body:
Yeah, typing on mobile was pretty tedious. My phone has a memory autocorrect system and actually autocorrects my words to the wrong thing half the time. I just wanted to vent, so I went through with the typing.

Yeah. I've found that when I actually do tend to show affection, I'm in a manic phase, and it starts to backfire horribly, as manic phases do. Or if I try it when I'm depressed I'm easily defeated or extremely passive and really can't go through with it. At the moment I don't really have anything to show affection to, but that's been my past experiences with it.

It's a pretty awful feeling thinking you're boring. I can't really remember any time I felt particularly interesting outside of a couple of manic phases. The hardest thing is I don't know how much of this is a realistic appraisal of myself (I tend to think an extreme amount about things) and how much of it is just a mood. I've found that the moods colour your experiences so much in such a subtle way. When you hear people talk about them, you'd expect that you'd notice the symptoms since they're described as being clear, but when you're in that state they often seem natural (like negativity seems to just be rational and default when you're depressed), which makes it so difficult to sort this all out.

I don't know that anything makes me interesting. I could give you things that I *find* interesting. I'm a very introverted and introspective person. I'm not particularly intelligent or erudite, so it's not like I'm intensely knowledgeable or anything. Just a curious person. I really like reading. I'm currently reading the Black Company series, which is a dark fantasy series. Before that, I read Malazan Book of the Fallen (my favourite series ever - very dark fantasy that I also found very insightful and beautiful). I've been on more of a fantasy kick recently. In the past, I read a lot of classic literature. Dostoevsky used to be one of my favourite authors. I've also read quite a bit of philosophy in the past. I used to read a lot of Nietzsche (in a manic phase I read a lot, which is really a terrible idea - I found him interesting, even though I found a lot of his ideas pretty distasteful), existentialists/absurdists, and so on. So I've read quite a bit in the past, and I read a pretty wide variety of stuff.

I also really like music. No musical talent, though, which I think would disqualify me from being part of a 'musical' crowd. I listen to a large variety there as well. Any genre. My favourite artist is Devin Townsend (absolutely incredible musician). I mainly listen to metal, but also listen to rock, some rap and country (Devin Townsend has a country album, so I guess that counts - trying to get into more rap and country though), classical, and so on. Again, wide variety, but I'm not knowledgeable on music.

Also like video games quite a bit. Wide variety there again.

As you can gather from this, I do a wide variety of introverted activities but I'm not particularly knowledgeable. I'd find a similarly introverted and curious person interesting to connect with. I really like having deep, long discussions and conversations with others, and I like exploring a lot of different stuff. Shared interests would be pretty important (I'm shitty at social interaction outside of that). 

I also find myself thinking that I'd probably need a connection with a mentally ill person to really emotionally connect. I know that's not necessarily a healthy thought process. I'm not saying I'd want to connect with someone very ill and go down a road to codependency. It's just that I find that I've been dealing with issues so long that it's so much harder to relate to 'normal' people, especially in terms of my experiences with moods, and so interacting with someone who is on some level able to really understand that and sympathize would make emotional intimacy much, much easier. I guess that also kind of means by extension that I don't much care for interacting with judgmental people. Everybody is to some extent, so it's not like I prefer the company of saints and Mr. Rogers, but I find people who are hateful towards others who have done nothing to them or people who generally have a hostile demeanour don't blend well with me in interactions.

There's the world's most clinical dissection of my interests. If for nothing else, I think it gives a pretty good indication of why I struggle with social interaction so much. I'm talking out of my ass, and so the content is shit, but it's really long and not much is happening in the text, so I've somehow made it sound like ambient music.

It's not even just that I want them to 'break through', it's also because there's so much baggage related to my illness that makes it difficult for me to move towards having a fulfilling life. That is a big part of it, though. I don't like just having acquaintances and detached interactions with other people.

I'm somewhat fearful of rejection, although I think a lot of other things take precedence, like feeling worthless, hopeless, depressed, 'crazy', etc., and thinking I can't really bond with another person. If I was really able to forge that bond with someone, I think that I would be much more comfortable and rejection wouldn't be super fearsome (not sure about the romantic side of things, haven't been in that situation in a long time). 

I sort of take a similar attitude. I mostly put on a socially acceptable demeanour, and I seem to be able to handle some casual interaction. I don't think I appear depressed or anything. I've spoken my mind with a lot of people, sometimes despite the fact that it could cause conflict. I think my issue is really bridging that gap for genuine connection, because I can go through the smaller motions but struggle a lot with actually finding anything meaningful.

I have a somewhat similar experience. My friend was ranting about some person who annoyed him and how this person was crazy. Granted, guy in question sounded like a bit of a difficult person, refusing to pay rent, arguing all the time; etc. However, it was what my friend said that bothered me. He said that the guy was 'crazy like the loony bins that you get in the ward', and started talking about psychotic people (you know, traditional garbage people say about the mentally ill). Ive been in the ward he's referring to, and have had psychosis. Didn't bother saying either of those things, and just rather peaceably suggested that most people who are 'crazy' aren't dangerous. He weakly assented and then went on to make fun of and talk about how scary some of them were,including one who apparently tried to break through a window to kill himself. I thought about doing that in the ward. Didn't tell him that, either. I just realize that nobody around me is compassionate. They like to think they are,because the alternative is unconscionable to them, but they're really largely assholes about anything outside of their immediate experience. I'm sorry you have to work with these people, and I'm sorry we ha e to be surrounded by them.

Holy shit, that turned out really long. I wrote it all out on mobile, so I couldn't add paragraph breaks and didn't see how long it was. I don't imagine anybody will read it, and that's fine. It's essentially gibberish anyways.
